tb21_profile.skill: Translate a stated hierarchical Bayesian model (Binomial likelihood, Beta group priors, improper (alpha+beta)^-5/2 hyperprior) into a probabilistic-programming model, drive an MCMC sampler with prescribed chains/iterations/seed, and report posterior means accurately
tb21_profile.domain: Bayesian statistics / MCMC; R + Stan (RStan 2.32.7) with its C++ toolchain, i.e. numerical statistics in a compiled scientific stack
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-from-spec plus install-and-configure a pinned compiled toolchain; graded on numeric closeness of the posterior means

TMax-15K.reason: Beta-Binomial posterior sampled by Metropolis-Hastings and checked against the exact conjugate answer - the same likelihood, prior family and posterior-mean deliverable.
Binomial data with Beta prior, MH chain of 110k iterations with burn-in, and the posterior mean validated against the analytical value to 0.005.
Drive a library sampler (emcee) with prescribed walkers, steps, seed and burn-in, then report posterior means - structurally identical to the rstan::sampling recipe.
Random-walk MH for a Bayesian regression posterior with Gaussian priors, fixed seed and burn-in, cross-checked against the closed-form solution.
Build the scientific environment (venv, numpy/scipy/emcee), then fix the likelihood's integrator so the MCMC converges - install-plus-sample, like RStan plus toolchain.
Repair an emcee pipeline (solver, parallel pool), run 50 walkers with burn-in and write posterior means of three parameters to JSON.
Exactly the TB2.1 data shape: trials/successes grouped by group, Binomial likelihood with Beta(1,1) prior, posterior mean per group - but conjugate, no sampler.
MCMC posterior means differ run to run despite a fixed seed; teaches what actually makes a sampler reproducible, which TB2.1 demands via seed=1.
Fit initial estimates, run emcee or MH for the posterior of Tm, and report the posterior mean and credible interval from the chain.
Parallel MCMC with at least 4 chains/workers, uniform priors, burn-in discarded, posterior means written out - the multi-chain configuration TB2.1 specifies.

notes: Neither Stan nor R exists anywhere in the 56k pool: the only Rscript hit in any corpus is task_000640_34df4518 (a bash orchestration task that merely shells out to a provided bootstrap_ci.R), and searching for 'Stan'/'rstan' only matches the substring inside 'understand'. So domain scores here mean 'Bayesian/MCMC numerical statistics', not 'R+Stan'. TMax is by far the richest source - it has well over a hundred MCMC tasks - and I deliberately preferred the ones that run a sampler with a prescribed configuration and validate a posterior mean over the many closed-form Beta-Binomial conjugate chores, which share the vocabulary but skip the sampling skill entirely. Nothing in the pool has a genuinely hierarchical (partially pooled) model; 'hierarchical' in TMax always means trees or SQL recursion, so I ignored all 197 of those hits. SWE-Rebench is the only other strong corpus, via pymc / numpyro / gpflow / pyautofit. Recursive-Task-Synthesis has no Bayesian content at all - its ten are pinned-version scientific installs and seeded pipelines, and their overall scores of 2-3 are honest. The install-RStan-2.32.7 half of the task is best served by the conda/pinned-version and build-from-source items (rts_task_634e80a627f837bf3aa0b8e7, tw_528959, scikit-build-core-712), which I kept at low ranks rather than dropping.
